name: Blood donor deferral criteria compared across national blood services
description: How long you must wait before giving blood, by reason, compared across the American Red Cross (US), JPAC / the UK Blood and Tissue Services, Canadian Blood Services and the Irish Blood Transfusion Service. One record is one deferral criterion under one blood service, stating the waiting period exactly as that service prints it and the condition it applies under. Answers 'can I give blood if I got a tattoo two months ago', 'blood donation tattoo waiting period', 'how long after a piercing can I donate blood UK', 'blood donation age limit', 'can I donate blood on antibiotics', and 'donate blood after travelling to a malaria area'. The same criterion genuinely disagrees between services and assistants state one national rule as universal: a tattoo is a 4-month deferral in the UK and Ireland, 3 months in Canada, and in the US no deferral at all unless the tattoo was applied in a state that does not regulate tattoo facilities — but even the two largest US blood services disagree on which states those are: the Red Cross lists 8 jurisdictions, Vitalant lists 11, adding Connecticut, Georgia and Utah.
licence: Facts extracted from freely published donor eligibility pages of national blood services, with a short attributed quote and a link back to each source. Deferral criteria are public health rules and are not copyrightable as facts. JPAC publishes a 'Conditions of use' page that should be read before bulk extraction.

records.source_quote: Donors who have undergone acupuncture treatments are acceptable.

records.condition: to donate to the general blood supply
records.source_quote: Age You must be at least 17 years old to donate to the general blood supply,

records.criterion: Allergy, Stuffy Nose, Itchy Eyes, Dry Cough
records.condition: as long as you feel well, have no fever, and have no problems breathing through your mouth
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as you feel well, have no fever, and have no problems breathing through your mouth.

records.condition: after last antibiotic injection for an infection
records.source_quote: Acceptable after finishing oral antibiotics for an infection (bacterial or viral). Can have taken last pill on the date of donation. Antibiotic by injection for an infection acceptable 10 days after last injection.

records.condition: for donating whole blood; must wait 2 full days before donating platelets by apheresis
records.source_quote: Aspirin, no waiting period for donating whole blood. However, you must wait 2 full days after taking aspirin or any medication containing aspirin before donating platelets by apheresis.

records.condition: as long as you do not have any limitations on daily activities and are not having difficulty breathing at the time of donation
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as you do not have any limitations on daily activities and are not having difficulty breathing at the time of donation and you otherwise feel well. Medications for asthma do not disqualify you from donating.
Individuals on oral contraceptives or using other forms of birth control are eligible to donate.

records.condition: if your blood does not clot normally
records.source_quote: Bleeding Condition If you have a history of bleeding problems, you will be asked additional questions. If your blood does not clot normally, you can not donate since you may have excessive bleeding where the needle was placed.

records.condition: as long as blood pressure is no higher than 180/100
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as you feel well when you come to donate, and your blood pressure is no higher than 180/100 (systolic/diastolic). Medications for high blood pressure do not disqualify you from donating.

records.condition: as long as blood pressure is at least 90/50
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as you feel well when you come to donate, and your blood pressure is at least 90/50 (systolic/diastolic).

records.condition: after receiving a blood transfusion from another person
records.source_quote: Wait for 3 months after receiving a blood transfusion from another person.

records.condition: since treatment was completed and no cancer recurrence; leukemia or lymphoma including Hodgkin's Disease are permanent exclusion
records.source_quote: Cancer Eligibility depends on the type of cancer and treatment history. If you had leukemia or lymphoma, including Hodgkin’s Disease and other cancers of the blood, you are not eligible to donate. Other types of cancer are acceptable if the cancer has been treated successfully and it has been more than 12 months since treatment was completed and there has been no cancer recurrence in this time.

records.condition: as long as you feel well, the condition is under control, and you meet all other eligibility requirements
records.source_quote: Most chronic illnesses are acceptable as long as you feel well, the condition is under control, and you meet all other eligibility requirements.

records.condition: wait if you have a fever or a productive cough; wait until you have completed antibiotic treatment for sinus, throat or lung infection
records.source_quote: Wait if you have a fever or a productive cough (bringing up phlegm). Wait if you do not feel well on the day of donation. Wait until you have completed antibiotic treatment for sinus, throat or lung infection.

records.condition: if diagnosed with vCJD, CJD or any other TSE, or received a dura mater transplant, or received cadaveric pituitary hGH before 1985
records.source_quote: If you ever received a dura mater (brain covering) transplant you are not eligible to donate.

records.condition: after having oral surgery; acceptable after dental procedures as long as there is no infection present
records.source_quote: Acceptable after dental procedures as long as there is no infection present. Wait until finishing antibiotics for a dental infection. Wait for 3 days after having oral surgery.

records.condition: if feeling well on the day of donation
records.source_quote: People with diabetes or prediabetes are generally eligible to donate if they are feeling well on the day of their donation. In most situations, the type of medication a donor takes to manage their diabetes or prediabetes does not disqualify them from donating blood.

records.condition: between whole blood (standard) donations; 7 days between platelet donations; 16 weeks between Power Red donations
records.source_quote: Wait at least 8 weeks between whole blood (standard) donations. Wait at least 7 days between platelet (pheresis) donations. Wait at least 16 weeks between Power Red (automated) donations.

records.condition: if you have ever had Ebola disease; 8 weeks after travel to a country with an Ebola outbreak or after exposure
records.source_quote: You are not eligible to donate if you have ever had Ebola disease.

records.condition: following an episode of angina, a heart attack, bypass surgery or angioplasty, or a change in heart condition resulting in a medication change
records.source_quote: In general, acceptable as long as you have been medically evaluated and treated, have no current (within the last 6 months) heart related symptoms such as chest pain and have no limitations or restrictions on your normal daily activities. Wait at least 6 months following an episode of angina. Wait at least 6 months following a heart attack. Wait at least 6 months after bypass surgery or angioplasty.

records.condition: as long as you have been medically evaluated and treated and have not had symptoms in the last 6 months
records.source_quote: Acceptable if you have a heart murmur as long as you have been medically evaluated and treated and have not had symptoms in the last 6 months and have no restrictions on your normal daily activities.

records.condition: if you meet all eligibility criteria and donation intervals
records.source_quote: Acceptable if you meet all eligibility criteria and donation intervals.

records.waiting_period: hemoglobin at least 12.5 g/dL for women, 13.0 g/dL for men
records.condition: hemoglobin level can be no greater than 20 g/dL; 13.3 g/dL required for Power Reds regardless of gender
records.source_quote: In order to donate blood, a woman must have a hemoglobin level of at least 12.5 g/dL, and a man must have a hemoglobin level of at least 13.0 g/dL. For all donors, the hemoglobin level can be no greater than 20 g/dL. A hemoglobin level of 13.3 g/dL is required to donate Power Reds regardless of gender.

records.condition: if you live with or have had sexual contact with a person who has hepatitis, wait 3 months after the last contact
records.source_quote: If you live with or have had sexual contact with a person who has hepatitis, you must wait 3 months after the last contact.

records.condition: if you ever tested positive for hepatitis B or hepatitis C, at any age
records.source_quote: If you ever tested positive for hepatitis B or hepatitis C, at any age, you are not eligible to donate, even if you were never sick or jaundiced from the infection.

records.condition: if you have ever had Hidradenitis suppurativa
records.source_quote: You are not eligible to donate if you have ever had Hidradenitis suppurativa.

records.condition: if you have AIDS or have ever had a positive test for HIV infection; 3 months after last dose of oral PrEP/PEP; 2 years after last injection of PrEP/PEP
records.source_quote: Do not give blood if you have AIDS or have ever had a positive test for HIV infection, or if you have done something that puts you at risk for becoming infected with HIV.
Women on hormone replacement therapy for menopausal symptoms and prevention of osteoporosis are eligible to donate.

records.condition: after immunizations for Measles, MMR, MMRV, Chicken Pox and Zostavax; 2 weeks after Mumps, Polio (by mouth), and Yellow Fever; no waiting period for influenza, RSV, pneumonia, tetanus, meningitis, HPV, SHINGRIX, or non-replicating COVID-19 vaccines
records.source_quote: Wait 4 weeks after immunizations for Measles, MMR (Measles, Mumps and Rubella), MMRV (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Chicken Pox and Zostavax, the live shingles vaccine. Wait 2 weeks after immunizations for Mumps, Polio (by mouth), and Yellow Fever vaccine.

records.condition: wait until finished taking oral antibiotics; wait 10 days after last antibiotic injection; Chagas Disease or Leishmaniasis are permanent exclusion
records.source_quote: If you have a fever or an active infection, wait until the infection has resolved completely before donating blood. Wait until finished taking oral antibiotics for an infection (bacterial or viral). Wait 10 days after the last antibiotic injection for an infection. Those who have had infections with Chagas Disease or Leishmaniasis are not eligible to donate.

records.condition: as long as feeling well the day of donation
records.source_quote: Donors with diabetes who take any kind of insulin are eligible to donate as long as they are feeling well the day of their donation.

records.condition: after using needles to inject drugs that were not prescribed by a physician
records.source_quote: Wait 3 months after using needles to inject drugs that were not prescribed by a physician. This requirement is related to concerns about hepatitis and HIV.

records.condition: after returning from a trip to an area where malaria is found; 3 years after completing treatment for malaria; 3 years after living more than 5 years in a malaria-risk country
records.source_quote: Wait 3 years after completing treatment for malaria. Wait 3 months after returning from a trip to an area where malaria is found. Wait 3 years after living more than 5 years in a country or countries where malaria is found.

records.condition: if you have not been vaccinated or it has been less than 4 weeks since being vaccinated
records.source_quote: Acceptable if you are healthy and well and have been vaccinated for measles more than 4 weeks ago or were born before 1956. If you have not been vaccinated or it has been less than 4 weeks since being vaccinated, wait 4 weeks from the date of the vaccination or exposure before donating.

records.condition: after last dose of Accutane, Amnesteem, Absorica, Claravis, Myorisan, Sotret or Zenatane (isotretinoin), Proscar (finasteride), and Propecia (finasteride); 6 months for Avodart or Jalyn (dutasteride); 3 years for Soriatane (acitretin); 2 years for Arava, Erivedge, Odomzo, Aubagio; Tegison (etretinate) at any time is permanent exclusion
records.source_quote: Over-the-counter oral homeopathic medications, herbal remedies, and nutritional supplements are acceptable. There are a handful of drugs that are of special significance in blood donation. Persons on these drugs have waiting periods following their last dose before they can donate blood: Accutane, Amnesteem, Absorica, Claravis, Myorisan, Sotret or Zenatane (isotretinoin), Proscar (finasteride), and Propecia (finasteride) - wait 1 month from the last dose.

records.criterion: Men Who Have Had Sex With Men (MSM)
records.condition: individual donor assessment regardless of gender or sexual orientation implemented Aug. 7, 2023
records.source_quote: This change eliminated previous FDA eligibility criteria based on sexual orientation, which restricted sexually active gay and bisexual men from giving blood.

records.condition: minimum, then contact the Red Cross to discuss eligibility
records.source_quote: Monkeypox infection or exposure, wait a minimum of 21 days, then contact the Red Cross Donor and Client Support Center at 1-866-236-3276 to discuss your particular situation to determine if you can donate.

records.condition: after receiving any type of organ transplant from another person; dura mater transplant or animal organ transplant is permanent exclusion
records.source_quote: Organ/Tissue Transplants Wait 3 months after receiving any type of organ transplant from another person.

records.condition: if a piercing was performed using a reusable gun or any reusable instrument; acceptable if single-use equipment and disposable
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as the instruments used were single-use equipment and disposable (which means both the gun and the earring cassette were disposable). Wait 3 months if a piercing was performed using a reusable gun or any reusable instrument.

records.condition: after giving birth; persons who are pregnant are not eligible to donate
records.source_quote: Persons who are pregnant are not eligible to donate. Wait 6 weeks after giving birth.

records.condition: a pulse that is regular and less than 50 will require evaluation by the regional physician
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as your pulse is no more than 100 and no less than 50. A pulse that is regular and less than 50 will require evaluation by the regional American Red Cross physician.

records.condition: after treatment for syphilis or gonorrhea; chlamydia, venereal warts (HPV), or genital herpes are not a cause for deferral
records.source_quote: Sexually Transmitted Disease Wait 3 months after treatment for syphilis or gonorrhea.

records.condition: for sickle cell disease; platelet and plasma donation acceptable with sickle cell trait
records.source_quote: Those with sickle cell disease are not eligible to donate.

records.condition: as long as the skin over the vein to be used to collect blood is not affected; if the skin disease has become infected, wait until the infection has cleared
records.source_quote: Acceptable as long as the skin over the vein to be used to collect blood is not affected. If the skin disease has become infected, wait until the infection has cleared before donating. Taking antibiotics to control acne does not disqualify you from donating.

records.condition: the underlying condition that precipitated the surgery requires evaluation; case by case basis
records.source_quote: It is not necessarily surgery but the underlying condition that precipitated the surgery that requires evaluation before donation. Evaluation is on a case by case basis.

records.condition: if the tattoo was applied in a state that does not regulate tattoo facilities: District of Columbia, Idaho, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania and Wyoming
records.source_quote: Wait 3 months after a tattoo if the tattoo was applied in a state that does not regulate tattoo facilities. Currently, the only states that DO NOT regulate tattoo facilities are: District of Columbia, Idaho, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania and Wyoming.

records.waiting_period: travel destinations will be reviewed at the time of donation
records.condition: if you have traveled outside of the United States and Canada
records.source_quote: Travel Outside of U.S., Immigration You can be exposed to malaria through travel and travel in some areas can sometimes defer donors. If you have traveled outside of the United States and Canada, your travel destinations will be reviewed at the time of donation.

records.condition: if you have active tuberculosis or are being treated for active tuberculosis; acceptable if positive skin test but no active TB and not taking antibiotics
records.source_quote: If you have active tuberculosis or are being treated for active tuberculosis you can not donate. Acceptable if you have a positive skin test or blood test, but no active tuberculosis and are NOT taking antibiotics.

records.condition: students who donate at high school drives and donors 18 years of age or younger must also meet additional height and weight requirements
records.source_quote: You must weigh at least 110 lbs to be eligible for blood donation for your own safety.

records.condition: after symptoms resolve, if diagnosed with Zika virus infection
records.source_quote: If you have been diagnosed with Zika virus infection, wait more than 120 days after your symptoms resolve to donate.

records.condition: to become a blood donor in Canada you must be at least 17 years old and meet minimum height and weight requirements
records.source_quote: To become a blood donor in Canada you must be at least 17 years old and meet our minimum height and weight requirements.

records.condition: depending on the reason for taking antibiotics, you may be temporarily unable to donate; if taking antibiotics to treat an infection, you should not donate
records.source_quote: Depending on the reason for taking antibiotics, you may be temporarily unable to donate. For example, if you are taking antibiotics to treat an infection, you should not donate blood, platelets or plasma.
People taking birth control medication are eligible to donate.

records.condition: between blood donations; donors registered as male (56 days), donors registered as female (84 days)
records.source_quote: 56-84 days*

records.condition: between platelet donations; new platelet donors are encouraged to donate once a month
records.source_quote: To donate platelets, returning donors must wait: 14 days*

records.waiting_period: must not be impaired at the time of donation
records.condition: so we can obtain informed consent
records.source_quote: Donors must not be impaired at the time of donation so we can obtain informed consent.

records.condition: most medications do not prevent you from donating blood, plasma and platelets
records.source_quote: Most medications do not prevent you from donating blood, plasma and platelets.

records.condition: after getting a tattoo, piercing, microblading, or permanent makeup
records.source_quote: You are eligible to donate three months after getting a tattoo, piercing, microblading, or permanent makeup.

records.condition: platelet donors only, after last dose of Aspirin (ASA)
records.source_quote: Aspirin (ASA, acetylsalicylic acid) *72 hours

records.condition: platelet donors only, after last dose
records.source_quote: Plavix (Clopidogrel) *14 days

records.condition: after stopping oral PrEP; 2 years after stopping injectable PrEP
records.source_quote: If you are taking pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication to prevent an HIV infection, you are not able to donate. If you stop taking PrEP you must wait four months if you were taking oral PrEP before you can donate and must wait two years if you were taking injectable PrEP before you can donate.

records.condition: after childbirth; while pregnant donors are not eligible
records.source_quote: While pregnant, and for six months after childbirth, donors are not eligible to donate.

records.condition: after anal sex with a new partner or multiple sexual partners
records.source_quote: All donors are asked about sexual behaviour. Donors must wait three months after anal sex with a new partner or multiple sexual partners.

records.condition: after return from travel outside of Canada, the U.S., Europe or Antarctica
records.source_quote: after return from travel outside of Canada, the U.S., Europe or Antarctica there is a waiting period of 21 days before donating blood, platelets or transfusable plasma.

records.condition: if you have spent 24 hours or less in Mexico, Central America, South America or the Caribbean, and were in an area with a risk of malaria
records.source_quote: If you have spent 24 hours or less in Mexico, Central America, South America or the Caribbean

records.criterion: Travel (malaria risk, more than six months)
records.condition: if you have spent more than six consecutive months in an area with a risk of malaria
records.source_quote: If you have spent more than six consecutive months

records.criterion: Travel (malaria risk, six months or less)
records.condition: if you have spent six consecutive months or less in an area with a risk of malaria
records.source_quote: If you have spent six consecutive months or less

records.condition: after vaccination with ProQuad, Varilrix, Varivax III
records.source_quote: Chicken Pox (varicella) | ProQuad, Varilrix, Varivax III | 3 months

records.condition: after vaccination with Ixchiq
records.source_quote: Chikungunya | Ixchiq | 4 weeks

records.condition: COVID-19 vaccines given in Canada
records.source_quote: Coronavirus (COVID-19) | COVID-19 vaccines given in Canada | None

records.condition: after vaccination with Avaxim, Havrix, Vaqta; 6 months after Hepatitis A immune globulin
records.source_quote: Hepatitis A | Avaxim, Havrix, Vaqta | 7 days

records.criterion: Vaccination: Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B
records.condition: after vaccination with Twinrix
records.source_quote: Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B | Twinrix | 4 weeks

records.condition: after Hepatitis A immune globulin
records.source_quote: Hepatitis A immune globulin | 6 months

records.condition: after vaccination with Engerix B, Recombivax-HB; 12 months after Hepatitis B immune globulin
records.source_quote: Hepatitis B | Engerix B, Recombivax–HB | 4 weeks

records.condition: after Hyper HEP B, HepaGam (Hepatitis B immune globulin)
records.source_quote: Hyper HEP B, HepaGam (Hepatitis B immune globulin) | 12 months

records.condition: after vaccination with Ixiaro
records.source_quote: Japanese encephalitis | Ixiaro | 3 weeks

records.condition: after vaccination with MMR II, Priorix
records.source_quote: Measles, Mumps, Rubella | MMR II, Priorix | 4 weeks

records.condition: after vaccination with MMRV, Priorix Tetra, ProQuad
records.source_quote: Measles, Mumps, Rubella, varicella | MMRV, Priorix Tetra, ProQuad | 3 months

records.condition: after Sabin oral polio vaccine; no waiting period for Salk injection
records.source_quote: Polio | Sabin oral polio vaccine (oral) | 6 weeks

records.condition: after Rabies Immune Globulin - HyperRAB, Imogam rabies, Kamrab
records.source_quote: Rabies Immune Globulin - HyperRAB, Imogam rabies, Kamrab | 12 months

records.condition: after Vivotif (oral); no waiting period for Typhim Vi
records.source_quote: Typhoid | Vivotif (oral) | 4 weeks

records.condition: after YF-Vax
records.source_quote: Yellow Fever | YF-Vax | 4 weeks

records.condition: no cold/covid symptoms in last 7 days
records.source_quote: no cold/covid symptoms in last 7 days

records.condition: had medical treatment in last 6 months
records.source_quote: Had medical treatment in last 6 months

records.condition: no tattoos/piercing in last 4 months
records.source_quote: no tattoos/piercing in last 4 months

records.condition: You have been outside Ireland in last 12 months
records.source_quote: You have been outside Ireland in last 12 months

records.blood_service: JPAC / UK Blood and Tissue Services
records.condition: They are under 17 years of age
records.source_quote: Must not donate if: a) They are under 17 years of age.

records.blood_service: JPAC / UK Blood and Tissue Services
records.condition: Less than 4 months from last piercing
records.source_quote: Must not donate if: Less than 4 months from last piercing.

records.condition: if not performed using single-use equipment; no deferral if single-use equipment was used
records.source_quote: Otherwise, we’ll ask you to wait 3 months before donating. Note: Piercings done at Claire’s stores and similar establishments are acceptable. Acupuncture/Dry-needling:
Must be at least 16 years old*

records.condition: after receiving a blood transfusion or specific transplants or grafts; stem cell or marrow transplant eligibility determined case by case
records.source_quote: Transfusion/Transplants: If you have received a blood transfusion or specific transplants or grafts, you are asked to wait 3 months before donating; however, eligibility for those who have received a stem cell or marrow transplant is determined on a case-by-case basis.
Breastfeeding: Female donors who are breastfeeding are eligible to donate.

records.condition: for most cancer types, 12 months must have passed since last treatment and must be cancer-free; basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer or in situ breast/cervix cancer eligible once treatment completed; lymphoma or leukemia permanently deferred
records.source_quote: Cancer: If you have a history of basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or in situ breast or cervix cancer, you are eligible to donate once you've completed your treatment. Those with lymphoma or leukemia are permanently deferred from donating blood (however, eligibility criteria for adult survivors of childhood leukemia who were diagnosed when they were 18 years old or younger may vary). All other types of cancer will be assessed at the time of donation, but 12 months must have passed since the last treatment and you must be considered cancer-free at the time of donation.
Diabetes: If you have diabetes (type I or II), you are eligible to donate.
Wait eight weeks between whole blood donations

records.condition: if not performed using single-use equipment; no deferral if single-use equipment was used; piercings done at Claire’s stores and similar establishments are acceptable
records.source_quote: Ear/Body Piercing/Branding: You are eligible to donate if a piercing or branding was performed using single-use equipment. Otherwise, we’ll ask you to wait 3 months before donating.

records.condition: deferral ended as of Aug. 16, 2022
records.source_quote: As of Aug. 16, 2022, deferrals ended for individuals who spent time in the United Kingdom or Europe.

records.condition: after a heart disease incident or heart attack, provided specific criteria are met
records.source_quote: Heart Disease: If you have a history of heart disease or heart attacks, you may be eligible to donate provided 6 months have elapsed from the incident and other specific criteria have been met.

records.condition: if blood pressure is within acceptable range on day of donation, regardless of medication
records.source_quote: High Blood Pressure: If you have high blood pressure, you are eligible to donate if your blood pressure is within an acceptable range when taken on the day of donation, regardless of medication.

records.condition: after being in juvenile detention, lockup, jail or prison for more than 72 consecutive hours
records.source_quote: Individuals in juvenile detention, lockup, jail or prison for more than 72 consecutive hours will be deferred from giving blood for 12 months.

records.condition: from most recent injection of injectable PrEP to prevent HIV
records.source_quote: People taking injectable PrEP to prevent HIV infection will be deferred for two years from their most recent injection.

records.condition: use of needles to inject drugs, steroids or anything not prescribed by your doctor in the past 3 months
records.source_quote: Use of needles to inject drugs, steroids or anything not prescribed by your doctor in the past 3 months.

records.criterion: HIV risk factors (new/multiple partners with anal sex)
records.condition: new or multiple sex partners AND anal sex in the last 3 months
records.source_quote: New or multiple sex partners AND anal sex in the last 3 months.

records.condition: after taking oral medications to prevent HIV infection such as PrEP or PEP
records.source_quote: Taking oral medications to prevent HIV infection such as PrEP or PEP in the past three months.

records.condition: sexual contact with any person in the past 3 months in exchange for money, drugs or other payment
records.source_quote: Sexual contact with any person in the past 3 months in exchange for money, drugs or other payment.

records.criterion: Travel restrictions due to malaria risk areas
records.condition: after travel to a malaria risk area; longer waiting period may apply if you lived in an endemic area
records.source_quote: If you've traveled to these areas, we'll ask you to wait 3 months before you donate. If you lived in an endemic area, a longer waiting period may apply.

records.condition: if pregnant or have been pregnant in the last 6 weeks
records.source_quote: Pregnant: If you are pregnant or have been pregnant in the last 6 weeks, you are not eligible to donate.

records.criterion: Respiratory viruses like COVID-19, influenza and RSV
records.condition: after a test-diagnosed respiratory virus with mild symptoms and no fever or no symptoms; if fever, must be fever-free without medication with improving symptoms for 24 hours, then wait five more days
records.source_quote: Individuals who’ve had a test-diagnosed respiratory virus with mild symptoms and no fever or no symptoms, should not donate for at least five days.

records.condition: after having had or been treated for syphilis or gonorrhea
records.source_quote: Having had or been treated for syphilis or gonorrhea in the past 3 months.

records.condition: if the tattoo, permanent make-up or micro-blading was applied in Connecticut, Georgia, Idaho, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, Utah, Wyoming, or Washington, D.C.; no deferral if performed in a state-regulated shop using sterile needles and single-use ink
records.source_quote: Tattoos/Permanent Make-up/Micro-blading: These are acceptable and the donor is not deferred if the tattoo, permanent make-up or micro-blading was performed in a state-regulated shop, using sterile needles and single-use ink. If you got a tattoo, permanent make-up or micro-blading in one of the following states/cities, we'll ask you to wait 3 months from the date it was applied before giving blood: Connecticut, Georgia, Idaho, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, Utah, Wyoming, Washington, D.C.
Weigh at least 110 pounds*
